correctness.rationale: For every finite n>=2, conditioning on the tagged interval, the neighbor-clique condition is equivalent to absence of an interior right endpoint before an interior left endpoint. Partitioning by the unique final interior left endpoint yields the exact integral. For scaled short intervals, multinomial endpoint counts yield independent left/right Poisson point fields with explicit rates; factorial moment measures give vague marked PPP convergence, and a uniform two-block exponential probability bound removes the length cutoff in any fixed interior position band. Integrating intensity gives logarithmic mean; an exact inclusion-exclusion on no-interior-endpoint sets gives the harmonic lower bound. Finite verifier run from current package passed 67,598 assertions including all endpoint pairings through six intervals and nine exact conditional-integral cases. The tests alone are explicitly not treated as proof of infinite statements.

originality.rationale: Searches for the local neighbor-clique/simplicial event, its endpoint-order equivalence, Poisson count and marked interval-length spectrum found no explicit equivalent or stronger result. The two accessible same-model full texts were checked at their relevant chapters/theorems; one establishes dense graph limits/degree and clique laws, the other surveys degrees, cliques and independence, without an implication covering this rare spatial point process. A published near-complete ER simpliciality result has a different dependence model; same-model component–coverage covariance concerns another functional. The original 1988 full text was inaccessible, so residual priority uncertainty is recorded, not concealed.

No automated search can establish global historical priority; an unidentified general Poisson-process theorem might subsume parts of the result, though no decisive dominating implication was found.

value.rationale: Simplicial vertices are the elementary removable vertices in chordal/interval-graph elimination, so their local abundance and geometry matter for sparse-elimination ordering and for local structural inference. The new law is spatially inhomogeneous (integrable on strict interior bands but singular at domain boundaries) and gives exact location and rescaled-length marks, not merely a routine global mean. The logarithmic exact band intensity and independent band counts identify a natural interior sampling law and expose a boundary-dominated distinction. A finite conditional law provides independent access to verification and further refinements. The work does not claim a full global count distribution, speed of convergence, or automatic algorithmic consequence.
